findings.title: S1 pin 1 is a supply pin sharing /ECHO with the MCU port U2.39
findings.why: /ECHO carries both a power input and a general-purpose pin. Either the port is being asked to source a rail, or the rail is backfeeding the port through its protection diode. Neither part survives that for long.
findings.fix: Return S1 pin 1 to its supply net and leave /ECHO to the signal.

findings.title: S1 pin 1 (GND_1) is on /ECHO, not GND

findings.title: S1 pin 1 is a supply pin sharing /ECHO with the MCU port U2.39
findings.why: /ECHO carries both a power input and a general-purpose pin. Either the port is being asked to source a rail, or the rail is backfeeding the port through its protection diode. Neither part survives that for long.
findings.fix: Return S1 pin 1 to its supply net and leave /ECHO to the signal.

findings.title: S1 pin 1 (GND_1) is on /ECHO, not GND
findings.why: The part names this pin GND, and the board has a net called GND. Wiring it to /ECHO instead means the pin is doing a different job than the symbol says it does.

findings.title: S1 pin 1 is a supply pin sharing /ECHO with the MCU port U2.39
findings.why: /ECHO carries both a power input and a general-purpose pin. Either the port is being asked to source a rail, or the rail is backfeeding the port through its protection diode. Neither part survives that for long.
findings.fix: Return S1 pin 1 to its supply net and leave /ECHO to the signal.

findings.title: S1 pin 1 (GND_1) is on /ECHO, not GND
findings.why: The part names this pin GND, and the board has a net called GND. Wiring it to /ECHO instead means the pin is doing a different job than the symbol says it does.
findings.fix: Move S1 pin 1 back to GND.

findings.title: S1 pin 1 is a supply pin sharing /ECHO with the MCU port U2.39
findings.why: /ECHO carries both a power input and a general-purpose pin. Either the port is being asked to source a rail, or the rail is backfeeding the port through its protection diode. Neither part survives that for long.
findings.fix: Return S1 pin 1 to its supply net and leave /ECHO to the signal.

findings.title: No copper track on /VIN_LDO net
findings.why: The LDO input pins are not electrically connected, so the regulator cannot receive power
findings.fix: Add a copper trace on the appropriate layer to connect all pins of the /VIN_LDO net

findings.title: No copper track on VBUS net
findings.why: USB VBUS is not routed to the protection diode, preventing power from reaching the USB connector
findings.fix: Route a copper trace between D1.2 and J10.1 on the appropriate layer

findings.title: Decoupling capacitor C2 is 7.4 mm from U1.2(VO)
findings.why: Excessive distance can reduce the effectiveness of high‑frequency decoupling
findings.fix: Place C2 closer to the VO pin or add an additional capacitor nearer to the pin

findings.title: Decoupling capacitor C1 is 8.2 mm from U1.3(VI)
findings.why: Large distance may limit the capacitor's ability to filter input transients
findings.fix: Move C1 closer to the VI pin or add a supplemental capacitor near the pin

findings.title: VBUS is not one piece of copper: 2 separate islands, 1 pads stranded
findings.why: The netlist says these pads are one net and the copper says otherwise. Nothing in ERC or DRC reads the copper, so both pass a board that cannot work.
findings.fix: Stitch the VBUS islands together: vias between the layers where the pads are, and a pour on both.

findings.title: No decoupling capacitor is listed on the +5V net
findings.why: Without local decoupling the +5V rail may experience voltage droop and noise affecting downstream circuits
findings.fix: Place one or more ceramic decoupling capacitors (e.g., 0.1 µF) close to the power pins of devices on the +5V net

findings.title: No decoupling capacitor is listed on the +3.3VA analog supply net
findings.why: The analog supply lacks local decoupling, which can introduce noise into analog peripherals
findings.fix: Add appropriate ceramic decoupling capacitors (e.g., 0.1 µF) near the analog supply pins

findings.title: The feedback net (/FB) of the buck regulator has no decoupling capacitor
findings.why: A missing capacitor on the feedback node can cause instability or poor regulation of the buck converter
findings.fix: Add a small capacitor (e.g., 10 nF) from the /FB net to ground close to the regulator feedback pin

findings.title: NRST pin has no pull‑up resistor to +3.3 V
findings.why: The MCU reset input may float, preventing reliable reset and programming
findings.fix: Add a 10 kΩ resistor from /NRST to +3.3 V

findings.title: BOOT0 pull‑down resistor is not tied to ground
findings.why: BOOT0 can float, causing unpredictable boot mode selection
findings.fix: Connect the other end of R4.2 to GND (or replace with a proper pull‑down resistor to GND)

coverage.decoupling_distance: measured, reported as evidence rather than as a finding

findings.title: R1 has value "R", which is not a quantity
findings.why: There is no magnitude here, so the line cannot be ordered and nobody assembling the board knows what to fit.
findings.fix: Give R1 a value that can be ordered.

findings.title: +5V net has no decoupling capacitor listed
findings.why: Absence of local decoupling can cause voltage transients and instability on the 5 V rail
findings.fix: Add a low‑ESR decoupling capacitor (e.g., 0.1 µF) close to the +5V pins of U1 and the diode outputs

findings.title: Decoupling capacitor C2 is 7.4 mm away from U1 VO pin
findings.why: Excessive distance reduces the effectiveness of high‑frequency decoupling
findings.fix: Place a decoupling capacitor (e.g., 0.1 µF) within ~5 mm of the U1 VO pin

findings.title: Decoupling capacitor C1 is 8.2 mm away from U1 VI pin
findings.why: Large separation can allow noise on the input rail to reach the regulator
findings.fix: Move C1 closer to the U1 VI pin or add an additional capacitor near the pin

findings.title: Decoupling capacitor C3 is 6.8 mm away from the ferrite bead ground pin
findings.why: Long ground return path can diminish the ferrite bead’s filtering effectiveness
findings.fix: Place a decoupling capacitor closer to S1.1 or add a via stitching to shorten the ground path

findings.title: NRST pin has only a capacitor to ground and no pull‑up resistor to +3.3 V
findings.why: The reset line may float and not reliably reset the MCU
findings.fix: Add a pull‑up resistor (e.g., 10 k) from /NRST to +3.3 V

findings.title: Buck regulator enable pin (EN) is tied to the VIN net
findings.why: The regulator is permanently enabled and cannot be turned off by firmware
findings.fix: Separate EN onto its own control net and drive it with a GPIO or switch

findings.title: ULN2003 ground pin lacks a nearby decoupling capacitor (C16 is 17.2 mm away)
findings.why: Insufficient local bypass may cause noise on the ULN2003 inputs
findings.fix: Place a small bypass capacitor (e.g., 0.1 µF) close to U3.8

findings.title: Feedback divider R1/R2 is not referenced to ground; R2 connects to /FB instead of GND
findings.why: The regulator's feedback network will not see a proper reference, leading to incorrect output voltage or failure to regulate
findings.fix: Connect R2.2 to the GND net (or move R2 to GND) so the divider spans VOUT to GND

findings.title: Decoupling capacitor C2 is placed between SW and VBST nets instead of to ground
findings.why: This unconventional connection can cause instability or oscillation of the switching regulator
findings.fix: Reconnect C2 so one side is on the VBST net and the other side is on GND (or place a capacitor between SW and GND as per the regulator datasheet)

findings.title: Bootstrap diode from VIN to VBST is missing
findings.why: Without the diode the bootstrap capacitor cannot charge, preventing the high‑side MOSFET from turning on and causing the converter to fail to start
findings.fix: Add a Schottky diode (e.g., 1N5819) from the VIN net to the VBST net
